description: NLP Prompt Compressor for LLMs. Reduces token usage by up to 70% using semantic contraction across 50+ languages. Licensed under the Caveman License (MIT + mandatory attribution to Passaro Francesco Paolo - Digitalsolutions.it). Bundled language data derived from Universal Dependencies (see NOTICE).
releaseNotes: 1.5.1: Words that carry the meaning of a request are never removed. Negations and query vocabulary now come from per-language data (54 languages, new embedded keep dictionaries): negations (curated for 16 languages), and query words such as interrogatives, quantifiers, comparisons, time and range words (before, after, since, until, between, dopo, dal, fino, entro, senza, at least, almeno) plus numerals, units of time, months, weekdays, aggregation and sorting words; Italian and English ship more than 1500 each. Any word next to a number or a date (two before, one after) is kept, so limits such as "more than 65 years" or "after 2022" survive. XML/HTML-style tags (for example the thinking and response tags used in prompts) are isolated as protected tokens and survive verbatim. The package is less than half the size (about 68 MB instead of 149 MB): the embedded document-frequency tables no longer carry terms that appear in fewer than 6 reference documents. 1.5.0: CavemanSemanticCache (algorithmic, multilingual, protected tokens for files/numbers/identifiers); chats compress JSON, XML, HTML, Markdown, SQL and code instead of stripping them; tool calls and tool results are never removed or altered (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Bedrock Converse, Gemini, Cohere and text formats of Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Llama, GLM); ToStrictAlternation / ToConverseMessagesJson for Amazon Bedrock Converse (Nova); XML content type; token counting for Gemini, Qwen, DeepSeek, Grok, GLM, Spark, Mistral, Nova, Kimi, Ernie, Command; targets .NET 10. 1.4.6: An inline JSON-object example embedded in prose (e.g. an instruction telling the model to answer with {"foo":"bar"}) is now isolated as a protected token, the same way a URL or IP address already was, so the literal braces/quotes/colons survive every compression level instead of being torn apart by the word filters. Only brace spans that contain at least one quoted string are protected (up to one level of nesting), so ordinary prose using curly braces for other reasons is unaffected. 1.4.5: Synthelion 1.2.5 fixes ported. (1) Structured values (IPs, versions, dates, URLs, e-mails, grouped decimals, percentages) survive every compression level. (2) Chinese/Japanese output is no longer longer than the input. (3) Indentation-based languages (Python, Ruby, shell) are detected as code. (4) Comment stripping is string-aware: it never cuts inside a string literal. (5) Structured-content guard: JSON, code, SQL, HTML, diffs and tables are routed to their structure-aware compressors and YAML/config is returned unchanged instead of being corrupted by the word filters. 1.4.4: Synthelion 1.2.5 feature port. (1) Numeric tokens preserved across every compression level — Semantic/Aggressive/Statistical/Syntactic previously dropped ports, amounts, percentages, versions, dates and temperatures; numbers are now always retained verbatim (never lemmatised). (2) New global-IDF provider and tables: 56 per-language {iso3}.idf.br document-frequency tables (built from Wikipedia, shipped as embedded brotli like the other worddata — same tables as Synthelion 1.2.5, ~128 MB) blended 50/50 into the Statistical level's TF-IDF scoring so word importance is grounded in real-world rarity, and used by Aggressive to additionally drop words ubiquitous in >50% of the reference corpus. Languages without a table fall back to the exact 1.4.3 local-only behavior. (3) SQL-aware compression: new CavemanSqlCompressor — SQL is auto-detected (ContentType.Sql) and routed away from the NLP path into a lossless whitespace/formatting collapse that protects keywords, string/numeric literals, quoted identifiers and comments; optional VALUES-tuple folding (lossy, CCR-hashed) mirrors CavemanJsonCrusher's row-drop. All changes additive and backward-compatible. Includes full 1.4.2/1.4.3 history below: 1.4.3 was a corrective re-publish of 1.4.2 (previously the 1.4.2 NuGet package was packed from a stale snapshot missing 1.4.0/1.4.1 features), carrying the language-quality pass ported back from Synthelion 1.2.0, negation-particle protection (eng/ita/fra/spa/deu/por/zho), the Italian "subito" ADV-homograph lemma fix, CavemanCjkSegmenter (jieba-style dictionary Chinese segmentation), mojibake repair in worddata/zho* and 10 further languages, and language-detection data contamination fixes ("john"/"ha"/"e"/"ate").
